title: Amateur

description.main: Fabian Reimann's Amateur (Spector Books / Kunstverein Hannover, 2013) draws on FBI archive photographs of the studio and workspace of the Soviet spy Rudolph Abel, who painted and photographed as an amateur artist under cover. 116 pages, English and German.
description.extended:
Fabian Reimann's Amateur uses FBI archive photographs to look at the studio of the Soviet spy Rudolph Abel, whose cover as an amateur artist was fifty oil paintings.

When Abel (1903–1971) was arrested in New York on 21 June 1957, agents found the paintings in his studio. He had used his work as an amateur painter and photographer as cover, and his favourite subject was lonely old men in the big city. Reimann researched the case in the FBI's archives. The pictures the agency took of Abel's studio and workspace show a man as adept at priming canvas as at making wiretaps. The book is a 116-page stitched, gatefolded brochure with illustrations, in English and German, designed by Florian Lamm and edited by Kunstverein Hannover.

The book was published in March 2013 by Spector Books, Leipzig, on the occasion of the exhibition Amateur und Überflieger at Kunstverein Hannover.
description.exhibition_context: Published on the occasion of the exhibition Amateur und Überflieger, Kunstverein Hannover, 2013.

notes: Spector Books lists the artist as Fabian Reimann and Kunstverein Hannover as editor. Cover is 277 × 375 px, the largest the publisher serves. No official artist site confirmed (fabianreimann.com is an industrial designer, not confirmed as the same person).
